title: The use of MPSS for whole-genome transcriptional analysis in Arabidopsis
notes: First-author Delaware identity anchor. PubMed/PMC metadata and DOI agree. MPSS signature classes and mapping constraints are method context, not miRNA identity proof. No correction, retraction, or expression-of-concern notice was displayed at retrieval.

title: Arabidopsis MPSS. An online resource for quantitative expression analysis
notes: Full name, Delaware affiliation and email resolve identity. The paper is a Meyers-team technology/database anchor, not independent validation. PubMed displayed no linked correction, retraction or expression of concern at retrieval.

title: Elucidation of the small RNA component of the transcriptome
notes: The journal record marks Meyers and Green as corresponding authors; team result, not a sole-author statement. Claims here are limited to PubMed/journal metadata and abstract because no authorized open full text was used. No correction/retraction notice was found in the checked records.

title: MicroRNAs and other small RNAs enriched in the Arabidopsis RNA-dependent RNA polymerase-2 mutant
notes: Meyers is final author; coauthored team finding. The paper explicitly notes unexplained enrichment for some candidates and uses genetic plus blot filters. PubMed/PMC showed no correction/retraction notice at retrieval.

title: An expression atlas of rice mRNAs and small RNAs
notes: Final-author, Delaware plant-genomics identity anchor. Only abstract-supported claims are used. Atlas abundance and genomic clustering do not alone establish biochemical function. No correction/retraction notice was displayed in PubMed at retrieval.

title: Endogenous siRNA and miRNA targets identified by sequencing of the Arabidopsis degradome
notes: No Meyers author. The Axtell/Bartel network later collaborated scientifically with Meyers, so this source is external concurrent support but is conservatively not counted as a strict network-independent laboratory item. It establishes convergent degradome methodology, not phenotype causality.

title: Global identification of microRNA-target RNA pairs by parallel analysis of RNA ends
notes: Meyers is a coauthor, not sole method owner. Abstract supports cleavage-site discovery in inflorescence and xrn4 libraries; PARE is not treated as phenotype causality. No correction/retraction notice was displayed in PubMed at retrieval.

title: MicroRNAs as master regulators of the plant NB-LRR defense gene family via the production of phased, trans-acting siRNAs
notes: Final-author team result. The title's 'master regulators' language is preserved as historical framing, not generalized beyond the tested NB-LRR networks. PubMed/PMC showed no correction/retraction notice at retrieval.

title: Phased, secondary, small interfering RNAs in posttranscriptional regulatory networks
notes: Author-written review supplies explicit uncertainty and open questions; it does not replace original evidence for specific mechanisms. PubMed/PMC showed no correction/retraction notice at retrieval.

title: An atlas of soybean small RNAs identifies phased siRNAs from hundreds of coding genes
notes: Meyers is final and corresponding author. The study separates PHAS-locus discovery, candidate triggers, miRNA annotation stringency, and predicted phasiRNA targets. PubMed/PMC showed no correction/retraction notice at retrieval.

title: Spatiotemporally dynamic, cell-type-dependent premeiotic and meiotic phasiRNAs in maize anthers
journal_or_venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
notes: Final-author/corresponding team result. Anther length, genotype, cell layer, and developmental stage are integral to interpretation. PubMed/PMC showed no correction/retraction notice at retrieval.

title: PhaseTank: genome-wide computational identification of phasiRNAs and their regulatory cascades
notes: Strict independent computational-method group with no Meyers author or identified collaboration-network overlap. The abstract supports tool scope and claimed benchmarking, not biological validation of each predicted cascade.

title: PMS1T, producing phased small-interfering RNAs, regulates photoperiod-sensitive male sterility in rice
journal_or_venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
notes: Meyers is a coauthor; Qifa Zhang is senior author. The paper supports PMS1T locus/phasiRNA/fertility causality in defined rice and photoperiod contexts while explicitly leaving downstream genes unresolved. PubMed/PMC showed no correction/retraction notice at retrieval.

title: Dynamic changes of small RNAs in rice spikelet development reveal specialized reproductive phasiRNA pathways
notes: Final-author identity verified by exact name, plant reproductive phasiRNA topic and recurrent coauthor network. PubMed status MEDLINE with no correction/retraction relation at retrieval.

title: unitas: the universal tool for annotation of small RNAs
notes: Strict independent Rosenkranz group. Figure-level benchmark compares unitas and PhaseTank and shows that background and abundance affect phased-RNA calls; software agreement is not biological truth.

title: PAREsnip2: a tool for high-throughput prediction of small RNA targets from degradome sequencing data using configurable targeting rules
notes: Strict independent Dalmay/Moulton method group. The paper explicitly warns that fixed rules derived from Arabidopsis can be overfit and become obsolete; a predicted PARE match remains rule- and transcriptome-dependent.

title: Revisiting Criteria for Plant MicroRNA Annotation in the Era of Big Data
notes: Two-author expert-written review; PubMed lists Meyers email and Danforth/Missouri affiliations. Criteria are author-explicit positions, while biological examples remain literature synthesis. No correction/retraction relation at retrieval.

title: 24-nt reproductive phasiRNAs are broadly present in angiosperms
notes: Co-corresponding team result. Broad presence is not universal presence; explicit absences and alternate trigger architectures are part of the result. PubMed/PMC showed no correction/retraction notice at retrieval.

title: Dicer-like 5 deficiency confers temperature-sensitive male sterility in maize
notes: Meyers and Walbot are corresponding authors. Genetic depletion of 24-nt phasiRNAs and fertility phenotypes are linked in dcl5 alleles, but the temperature dependence and tapetal context must be retained. PMC/Crossmark page showed no correction/retraction notice at retrieval.

title: miR2118-dependent U-rich phasiRNA production in rice anther wall development
notes: Strict independent Komiya/Nonomura network. Large MIR2118-cluster deletions, stage-resolved anther-wall phenotypes and small-RNA profiles support a somatic U-rich phasiRNA context distinct from MEL1-bound germ-cell phasiRNAs. AGO1b/d involvement is phrased as a proposed mechanism where direct loading evidence is incomplete.

title: 21-nt phasiRNAs direct target mRNA cleavage in rice male germ cells
notes: Independent-laboratory primary study used only to test whether the cleavage-evidence hierarchy generalizes beyond Meyers coauthorship. PubMed status MEDLINE with no correction/retraction relation at retrieval.

title: Reproductive phasiRNAs regulate reprogramming of gene expression and meiotic progression in rice
notes: Strict independent Yue-Qin Chen group. An Author Correction, DOI 10.1038/s41467-023-37355-6, published 2023-03-22, corrects Ke-Reng Zhou to Ke-Ren Zhou; it is bibliographic and does not report a change to the experimental conclusions. No retraction or expression of concern located.

title: Mechanism for the genomic and functional evolution of the MIR2118 family in the grass lineage
notes: Original external research with Xuemei Chen, a known Meyers collaborator, so it is not counted as strict network-independent. Control analyses support a specific critique that PARE searches over very large phasiRNA sets are prone to false-positive assignments. Legal publisher full text was readable, but a license-level open-access status was not verified.

title: 24-nt phasiRNAs move from tapetal to meiotic cells in maize anthers
notes: Meyers is a coauthor; team result. Spatial production and accumulation support tapetum-to-meiocyte mobility, while biological function remains explicitly uncertain. Legal publisher and accepted-manuscript full text were accessible, but a license-level open-access status was not verified. No correction/retraction notice was found.

title: Premeiotic 24-nt phasiRNAs are present in the Zea genus and unique in biogenesis mechanism and molecular function
journal_or_venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
notes: Meyers is final/co-corresponding author and contributed the paper. The article repeatedly uses probabilistic language for absent trigger/loading/cleavage evidence; these are not absolute biochemical exclusions. PMC/PubMed showed no correction/retraction notice at retrieval.

title: mRNA cleavage by 21-nucleotide phasiRNAs determines temperature-sensitive male sterility in rice
notes: Meyers is a coauthor rather than final author. The legal Oxford full article is reachable, but this N1 corpus used only abstract-supported conclusions; no additional figure-level claim was introduced during access correction. No PMCID was present in NCBI metadata and no correction/retraction relation was found.

title: Distinct classes of 21- and 24-nt phasiRNAs suggests diverse mechanisms of biogenesis and function in rice anther development
notes: Final-author identity is supported by UC Davis/Danforth affiliations and recurrent coauthors. The paper frames newly observed postmeiotic classes as a foundation for functional work rather than a completed mechanism. No correction/retraction relation at retrieval.

title: DICER-LIKE 5 loss causes thermosensitive male sterility in durum wheat and reveals an AU-rich motif guiding 24-nt phasiRNA biogenesis
journal_or_venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
notes: Final author with UC Davis and Danforth affiliations; identity continuity verified. Abstract and open PMC support cross-species comparison, non-miRNA motif initiation and allele rescue. No correction/retraction relation at retrieval.

title: Phased, secondary siRNAs in plant reproduction
journal_or_venue: Institute of Science and Technology Austria seminar
notes: Official ISTA page identifies Blake Meyers as speaker and provides an abstract, but no transcript or Q&A. `not_author` is the closest allowed project enum for an event page; the notes preserve his speaker role. It supports scope and explicit uncertainty only, not experimental details or response style.

title: Phased, secondary siRNAs in plant reproduction
journal_or_venue: Southern University of Science and Technology academic lecture
notes: Official event page verifies Blake Meyers as speaker, title, date (2026-02-05), and venue. `not_author` is the closest allowed project enum for an event page. No transcript, recording, abstract, or Q&A was available in the checked page; retained only as scope/timeline context and not used for a mechanistic claim.

title: Author Correction: Reproductive phasiRNAs regulate reprogramming of gene expression and meiotic progression in rice
notes: Dedicated publisher correction record. It changes the author spelling Ke-Reng Zhou to Ke-Ren Zhou and does not report altered data, figures, analyses or conclusions. Classified as `critique` because the fixed project source-type enum has no correction category; it is publication-status metadata, not a scientific critique or independent validation.
